clue.text: Bull holding the Spanish record used to summon Betjeman, perhaps

indicators.note: the bull holds the other pieces, so they sit inside its letters

parts.note: taken as the word itself
el is the Spanish word for the
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A curious picture of a bull clutching some Spanish record that somehow calls the poet John Betjeman.
explanation.walkthrough: John Betjeman's verse autobiography is titled 'Summoned by Bells', which is why a bell device could summon him.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord hung in a room that rings a bell to call servants, a device for summoning someone; Betjeman was famously summoned by bells.

clue.text: Tramp with a full glass

parts.note: a bum is a vagrant or tramp
per is Latin for by or with, as in 'per annum'

explanation.surface: A vagrant sitting with a brimming glass of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass filled to the brim, especially for a toast, is traditionally called by this name.

clue.text: Nasty smell after military turns up in prison

indicators.note: the smell comes after the other piece in the answer
in a down clue, turning up reads the word from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: BO is body odour

explanation.surface: An unpleasant odour lingers after soldiers arrive at a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal and older slang sense of the word is a prison or place of confinement.

clue.text: Pharaoh not unknown to join excellent holy man, a believer in old planetary system

definitions.text: a believer in old planetary system

indicators.note: not means without, so the unknown is taken away from the pharaoh

parts.note: Ptolemy was the name of the Greek dynasty of Egyptian pharaohs
Y is an algebraic unknown, like x and z
A1 means first-rate; written in crosswords as the letters A and I
ST is the abbreviation for a saint

explanation.surface: An Egyptian king teams up with a fine saint who believes in an old model of the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to join' simply links the pieces. A1 (excellent) is read as the letters AI.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Ptolemy's geocentric astronomy, in which the sun and planets circle the earth.

clue.text: Circuit where service changes sides and volumes

indicators.note: swapping one side for the other turns right into left, so the R becomes an L
a change of volume in music, loud to soft, makes forte into piano, so the F becomes a P

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A tennis match where the server swaps ends and the noise rises and falls.
explanation.walkthrough: Two changes: 'changes sides' turns R (right) into L (left), and 'volumes' turns F (forte, loud) into P (piano, soft), so RAF becomes LAP.
explanation.definitionFit: One complete trip round a racetrack or course is a single circuit.

clue.text: Fern-owls itch regularly in play

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the following words

explanation.surface: Nightjars, also called fern-owls, scratch themselves at intervals while at play.
explanation.walkthrough: A fern-owl is an old name for the nightjar bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To romp or play about in a lively, carefree way.

clue.text: Lady Bird left to stagger

parts.note: a ree, or reeve, is the female ruff, a wading bird

explanation.surface: A ladybird, or a lady named Bird, left to totter about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady Bird' looks like the insect or a First Lady, but it means a female bird: the ree.
explanation.definitionFit: To lurch or sway unsteadily on one's feet, as if dizzy or drunk.

clue.text: Thatcher's description of broken reed in unproductive bit of enterprise

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the other word

parts.note: lean years or lean times are unproductive ones

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters of reed are rearranged
a bit of the word is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher describing a feeble person inside a failing business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' makes DERE from REED, put 'in' LEAN; then E from 'bit of enterprise'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular term for a female leader, applied to Margaret Thatcher in the 1980s.

clue.text: Seal round a garden is something easily accomplished

indicators.note: round means the sealing word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: to calk, or caulk, is to seal joints against water
Kew Gardens is the famous botanic garden in London

explanation.surface: A seal or sealing compound placed around a garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW, the Royal Botanic Gardens in London, is the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, an easy victory or task is called this, after an old dance competition.

clue.text: Snake without tail used by old voodoo priestess

indicators.note: without its tail means the snake loses its final letter

parts.note: the mamba is a venomous African snake

explanation.surface: A voodoo priestess making use of a tailless snake in a ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: In Haitian vodou, a female priest is given this title.

clue.text: Before a meal the French judge dives into pack for brandy

parts.note: a.p. abbreviates ante prandium, Latin on prescriptions for before a meal

indicators.note: diving into something puts these pieces inside it

parts.note: taken as the word itself
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Before dinner, a French judge plunges into a pack to get some brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: AP comes from the prescription abbreviation 'ante prandium'.
explanation.definitionFit: An American spirit distilled from fermented cider, a type of apple brandy.

clue.text: Spiral outflow could be neatly conic

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A spiralling outward flow might be neatly cone-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-pressure weather system in which air spirals outward from its centre.

clue.text: Where to buy a slice of orange and a squirt of soda to put in Englishman's drink

indicators.note: these letters are placed inside the drink
and adds the second garnish into the drink as well as the first, at a separate spot

parts.note: a pint of ale is the stereotypical drink of an Englishman

indicators.note: a slice of the word is its opening letter
a squirt of the word is just its first letter

explanation.surface: A recipe: add a slice of orange and a dash of soda to an Englishman's beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The O and the S go into separate places: O after the P and S before ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: The place in a shop where payment is made, such as the checkout till.

clue.text: Finally, not altogether wealthy, I have small amount of money for caring for myself

indicators.note: finally places this piece at the very end of the answer

parts.note: the ego is the I, the self
a cent is a small coin

indicators.note: not altogether means not complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: rich means wealthy

explanation.surface: Someone not quite wealthy, with only a little money, ends up looking after themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-centred: concerned only with one's own interests and needs.

clue.text: First person's expression of pain is to cry

parts.note: me is a first-person pronoun
ow is what one says when hurt

explanation.surface: A person's own expression of pain is to weep.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's call, or to make that plaintive noise, as a feline does.

clue.text: Entertaining removal of decayed tapestries

indicators.note: decayed suggests the word has fallen apart and been reassembled

explanation.surface: Taking down tapestries that have rotted makes an amusing spectacle.
explanation.definitionFit: An erotic entertainment in which a performer takes off clothes one by one.

clue.text: Novel series of minute coaches made to fit in traffic

indicators.note: being caught up in traffic jumbles these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A sequence of tiny buses adapted to slot into the traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Powell's twelve-volume sequence of novels, a celebrated series of English fiction.

clue.text: Acknowledgement of violent sadism by Ionian? Not half

indicators.note: violent signals the letters are thrown into disorder
not half keeps only one half of the word, its first three letters

explanation.surface: An Ionian Greek makes an acknowledgement of violent sadism, or so the question suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A confession is an acknowledgement that something is true.

clue.text: Perch found occasionally in Gironde

indicators.note: occasionally means only some letters of the river name are kept, here an irregular selection

explanation.surface: A freshwater fish caught now and then in the Gironde estuary in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The selection is irregular: the 3rd, 4th and 6th letters of GIRONDE, an unusual construct.
explanation.definitionFit: An old unit of length of five and a half yards, also called a pole.

clue.text: Branch of technology beginning to reduce and almost stop involuntary movements

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter
almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: an oboe is a reed stop on an organ
tics are involuntary twitches

explanation.surface: A field of engineering that begins to curb and nearly halt involuntary twitches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stop' is an organ stop, not a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: The engineering field concerned with designing and building automated machines.

clue.text: Ken's returning to col in South Africa

indicators.note: returning means the name is read backwards

parts.note: the man's name Ken, taken as written

explanation.surface: Ken is heading back to a mountain pass in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Afrikaans word, used in South Africa, for a mountain pass or saddle between peaks.

clue.text: See 15 across
Month in France once without ecstasy relating to goddess

indicators.note: without means the drug's letter is taken out

parts.note: Floreal was the flower month of the French Revolutionary calendar
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A spring month in old France, free of drugs, connected with a goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora is the Roman goddess of flowers, so anything pertaining to her is flower-like.

clue.text: Supplant priceless French author

indicators.note: price-less means without the abbreviation for price

parts.note: Marcel Proust was the French novelist

explanation.surface: Displacing an invaluable French writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'priceless' seems to praise Proust; split it as price-less, removing PR, the abbreviation for price.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive out or force someone from a position, replacing them.

clue.text: Cloistered lama's tonic to be shaken

indicators.note: shaking mixes up the letters as in a cocktail

explanation.surface: A shut-away Tibetan monk's medicinal drink needs a good shake.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to monks or monastery life, secluded from the world.

clue.text: Priests get special rise for oath

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter rising means it moves up, earlier in the word

parts.note: curés are French parish priests

explanation.surface: Clergymen receive a special pay rise, promised under oath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' works only in a down clue: the S of CURES moves up one place.
explanation.definitionFit: A swear word or profane exclamation is an oath.

clue.text: Putting everything on Black can make Round object

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece placed on comes below, so after

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
all means everything

explanation.surface: Staking everything on black at the roulette table can win you a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere, such as the one rolling round the roulette wheel.

clue.text: I relieve one aged family of flags

parts.note: to rid someone of a burden is to relieve them
an ace counts as one in cards
AE abbreviates aetatis, Latin for aged, as on memorials

explanation.surface: Someone says they take care of a single elderly family of flag-wavers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flags' are the plants, irises, not banners.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical family of irises; flags are wild irises.

clue.text: Garment's about 454 grams

parts.note: A abbreviates about, as in approximate figures
a pound, LB, is about 454 grams

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing weighing roughly a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A long white vestment worn by priests at Mass.

clue.text: Clothes horse's demeanour in front of Queen

indicators.note: placed in front means it comes first

parts.note: an air is a manner or demeanour
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A fashion-conscious person's manner before the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes horse' looks like a vain dresser; it is the frame for drying laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: A folding frame on which washing is hung to dry indoors.

clue.text: Old Kentish river?

parts.note: Kent is in the south-east of England, SE
the Nile is the great African river

explanation.surface: Asking for an ancient river in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in South East England, abbreviated SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing the weakness of mind that can come with great age.

clue.text: Flower found in depressed ring

parts.note: blue means sad or depressed
a bell rings, and to give someone a bell is British slang for to phone

explanation.surface: A flower discovered inside a sunken ring of earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodland plant with drooping blue bell-shaped blooms.
